info.title: FinFlow API
info.description: All endpoints require an authenticated session (Flask-Login cookie, set by /login) and are scoped to the logged-in user's own accounts. State-changing requests (POST/PATCH/DELETE) also require a CSRF token, sent as header `X-CSRFToken` (get one from the `csrf-token` <meta> tag on any page, or the `csrf_token` hidden field on the login/signup forms).

200.description: A page of the caller's own transactions

is_fraud.description: Ground-truth fraud label (only ever set on generated data; used to evaluate the models). Never written by an import or the stream.

fraud_score.description: Calibrated 0-1 anomaly probability from the fraud model, set when the row was imported or streamed; null if unscored.

is_flagged.description: True if fraud_score >= the user's alert sensitivity (the same rule the Alerts page uses) or the row carries a ground-truth label.

patch.summary: Edit a transaction's category, optionally creating a standing rule

create_rule.description: If true, saves a standing rule for this merchant (for a UPI payment, the payee), re-categorizes all of this user's existing transactions with the same merchant identity, and applies the rule to future uploads.

transactions_updated.description: How many transactions changed category (1 unless a rule was created)

404.description: Transaction not found or not owned by this user

file.description: CSV, max 10MB. Columns are auto-detected (Date, Description/Narration, Amount or separate Debit/Credit columns); DD/MM/YYYY and Indian number formats are understood.

mapping.description: Optional JSON object of field -> column name, as reviewed by the user via /transactions/upload/preview. Which CSV column holds each field. Omit to use the auto-detected mapping (see suggested_mapping in the preview response). Optionally 'balance' (a running-balance column). Either 'amount', or 'debit' and/or 'credit', is required, plus 'date' and 'description'.

opening_balance.description: Optional number: the balance just before the first transaction in this file. Only used when the statement has no usable balance column and the file isn't later than what's already imported.

transactions_processed.description: Rows read from the file (after cleaning)

transactions_added.description: Rows that were new and saved

existing_account.description: True if the rows went into the user's existing imported account

opening_balance_source.description: statement = worked out from the file's balance column; user = typed by the user; unknown = no balance column, starts from 0; existing_account = file follows already-imported transactions, so the existing opening balance is kept

400.description: Missing file, wrong type, too large, unreadable CSV, unmappable columns, or a non-numeric opening_balance

post.description: All of a user's imported statements go into ONE account, so importing the same or an overlapping statement again only adds the rows that are new. Existing rows are never overwritten (a category the user corrected stays). The account's balance history is rebuilt from its opening balance plus all transactions.

post.summary: Simulate reducing spend in specific categories

reduce_categories.description: category_id -> reduction fraction (0-1). Keys are whitelisted against dim_category.

post.summary: Project a lump-sum investment at a blended return rate
Preview how a CSV would be read, without saving anything
post.description: Returns the detected column mapping, sample rows, the auto-assigned category for each transaction and a summary. If the mapping is unusable this still returns 200 with ready=false and an explanatory 'error', so a UI can let the user pick columns. Pass 'mapping' to re-preview with the user's corrections.

mapping.description: Optional JSON object of field -> column name.

opening_balance.description: Optional number: the balance just before the first transaction in this file. Only used when the statement has no usable balance column and the file isn't later than what's already imported.

suggested_mapping.description: Which CSV column holds each field. Omit to use the auto-detected mapping (see suggested_mapping in the preview response). Either 'amount', or 'debit' and/or 'credit', is required, plus 'date' and 'description'.

mapping.description: Which CSV column holds each field. Omit to use the auto-detected mapping (see suggested_mapping in the preview response). Either 'amount', or 'debit' and/or 'credit', is required, plus 'date' and 'description'.

ready.description: True if the mapping produced importable rows

already_imported.description: Rows in this file already imported (will be skipped)

new_rows.description: Rows that would actually be added

is_new.description: False if rows will be added to the user's existing imported account

opening_balance.description: Where the account's opening balance (the balance before its earliest transaction) comes from.

source.description: statement = worked out from the file's balance column; user = typed by the user; unknown = no balance column, starts from 0; existing_account = file follows already-imported transactions, so the existing opening balance is kept

editable.description: True when the user may supply their own opening balance
